changelog: **"Zoom to now" follows the owner's rule: a third of the view for the programme on air, two thirds for what runs before and after it, and the programme in the middle rather than wherever a fixed offset left it.** It used to give every programme a fixed 55% of the height whatever its length, which for a three-minute advert asked for some seven thousand pixels an hour, pinned the slider at its maximum and left one bar on the screen with nothing around it to say where in the evening it sat. There is a floor on context now - never less than about half an hour of schedule on screen - so a short programme takes less than its third and gets more neighbours than it asked for, which is the right way round. A programme longer than the view is still centred, but not so far that the now line leaves the screen.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
